confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for Seattle prices. Beer, coffee, restaurant meals and cocktails came from price aggregators, mainly Numbeo-derived data (Expatica, citing Numbeo data as of June 2026) plus Expatistan and MyLifeElsewhere. Several of those figures rest on few user-reported data points. Beer is about $8 for a 0.5L draught, with a $7 to $8 pint range elsewhere. Coffee is about $5.50 against reported $4.50 to $6 figures. The inexpensive meal is about $20 and the mid-range dinner for two is about $95, which sits between the $80 and $100 values reported. Cocktail is about $17, in line with the $16 to $22 range and the $18 downtown figure. I found no citywide average for restaurant wine by the glass. I set it at about $15 from a few venue examples (Tavern Law rosé at $16, Four Seasons sparkling at $18) and the wine-to-beer relationship, so it is the least certain drink anchor. The accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July 2026 peak season from general knowledge. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings. They are the least certain anchors and could vary widely by neighborhood and event demand. The FX rate comes from the search-result summary of the RBA exchange-rate pages, not from a page I read directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable city was used. Seattle prices were taken directly from US aggregator data for Seattle. Accommodation reflects Seattle's position as a high-cost West Coast city with strong summer tourism demand, similar to Portland and San Francisco but somewhat cheaper than San Francisco or New York for dining.
